task.situation: Your school magazine is planning an issue about learning. The editor has asked students to write articles about homework for teenage readers.
task.instruction: Write an article. In your article you should:
points: describe how homework can help students
explain what the limits of homework are
suggest how homework could work better

words.short: Give your article a title. Write around 200 words.
words.long: Give your article a title. Write around 250 words.

task.de: Artikel für die Schulzeitung zum Thema Hausübungen, Zielgruppe Jugendliche. Drei Inhaltspunkte: Nutzen beschreiben, Grenzen erklären, Verbesserungen vorschlagen. Den Titel wählen wir ganz zum Schluss.

focus.label: contrast linkers
focus.note: Marked: linking words that show a contrast or a concession (although, even though, even if, while, however, on the other hand, in contrast, though, even so, instead of, despite, yet). The simple ‘but’ is not marked.

gaps.q: Which student do we quote? First name only.
gaps.qDe: Ruft einen Vornamen für die Person, die wir zitieren. Keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen.

steps.q: How do we open the article and show what students think?
steps.de: Der erste Absatz macht neugierig auf das Thema Hausübungen und zeigt, was Schüler:innen darüber denken. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then finish the introduction in your own words: make readers curious and say what students think.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Einstieg mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben: neugierig machen und sagen, was Schüler:innen denken.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then finish the introduction in your own words: make readers curious and show both sides of what students think.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Einstieg mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben: neugierig machen und beide Seiten zeigen, was Schüler:innen denken.

options.label: Ask the readers a question
options.text: {{Do you ever sit at your desk}} late in the evening with a maths sheet that never ends? {{You are not alone.}} {{When we asked students in our year,}} some said short tasks help them before a test. {{[[In contrast,]] others}} complained that long projects eat up their weekends.
options.textLong: {{Do you ever sit at your desk}} late in the evening with a maths sheet that never ends? {{You are not alone, [[although]] some friends}} may claim they finish in ten minutes. {{When we asked students in our year,}} the answers were mixed. Some said short tasks help them before a test. {{[[In contrast,]] others}} complained that long projects eat up their weekends.
options.why: A question speaks to readers directly, and the quick survey shows that students do not agree.

options.label: Introduce the topic
options.text: Our school magazine has asked students to write articles about homework. In this article, I will describe how homework can help students, explain what the limits of homework are and suggest how homework could work better. Students in our year have different opinions about it.
options.textLong: Our school magazine has asked students to write articles about homework. In this article, I will describe how homework can help students, explain what the limits of homework are and suggest how homework could work better. We asked students in our year about it, and their opinions were very different. Some like short tasks before a test, but others hate long projects at the weekend.
options.reject: This copies the task almost word for word and gives readers no reason to read on. Use your own words and start with a hook.
options.rejectDe: Das ist fast wörtlich aus der Aufgabe abgeschrieben und macht niemanden neugierig. Eigene Worte und ein Einstieg, der packt.

options.label: Start with an argument at home
options.text: {{Few school topics cause as many arguments at home as}} homework. Parents see it as useful practice, [[while]] their children would rather meet their friends. {{“Some homework is really useful,” says}} {NAME}, a student in our year. “Three worksheets on a Friday afternoon, [[though,]] feel like a punishment.”
options.textLong: {{Few school topics cause as many arguments at home as}} homework. Parents often see it as useful practice, [[while]] their children would rather spend the afternoon with friends. {{“Some homework is really useful,” says}} {NAME}, a student in our year. “Three worksheets on a Friday afternoon, [[though,]] feel like a punishment.” {{But who is right?}} Both sides have a point.
options.why: Two opposite views and a student’s own words lead straight into the topic.

steps.q: Body paragraph 1: how can homework help students?
steps.de: Erster Inhaltspunkt: wie Hausübungen beim Lernen helfen können. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add one example of how homework helps and finish the last sentence.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann ein Beispiel ergänzen, wie Hausübungen helfen, und den letzten Satz fertigschreiben.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add two examples of how homework helps and finish the last sentence.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann zwei Beispiele ergänzen, wie Hausübungen helfen, und den letzten Satz fertigschreiben.

options.label: Practice before tests
options.text: {{To begin with, homework gives us time to practise}} what we learnt in class. New words and maths formulas only stay in our heads if we use them again. {{[[Even though]] it can be boring,}} this practice often makes tests easier.
options.textLong: {{To begin with, homework gives us time to practise}} what we learnt in class. New words and maths formulas only stay in our heads if we use them again. A few exercises at home also show us what we have not understood yet. {{[[Even though]] it can be boring,}} this practice often makes tests easier.
options.why: A clear topic sentence, examples and a result. ‘Even though’ admits the boring side.

options.label: Skills for life
options.text: {{For me, the biggest benefit of homework is}} the skills it teaches. By doing it regularly, we learn to plan our week, work alone and meet deadlines. {{These skills are useful [[even if]]}} we never use a maths formula again.
options.textLong: {{For me, the biggest benefit of homework is}} the skills it teaches. By doing it regularly, we learn to plan our week, work alone and meet deadlines. Nobody is there to tell us when to start, so we slowly become more independent. {{These skills are useful [[even if]]}} we never use a maths formula again.
options.why: Names the biggest benefit in the topic sentence and looks beyond marks.

options.label: Two ways it helps
options.text: Homework helps us in two ways. First, we practise new words and formulas until they stay in our heads. However, homework also teaches us to plan our week and meet deadlines. On the other hand, most teachers say these skills are important for later life.
options.textLong: Homework helps us in two ways. First, we practise new words and formulas until they stay in our heads, so tests on Friday feel much less scary. However, homework also teaches us to plan our week and meet deadlines. On the other hand, most teachers say these skills are important for later life and for every job.
options.reject: The linking words don’t fit: ‘However’ introduces a second benefit, not a contrast (→ In addition), and ‘On the other hand’ introduces a view that agrees (→ In fact).
options.rejectDe: Die Linking words passen nicht: However leitet einen zweiten Vorteil ein, keinen Gegensatz (→ In addition), und On the other hand leitet Zustimmung ein (→ In fact).

steps.q: Body paragraph 2: what are the limits of homework?
steps.de: Zweiter Inhaltspunkt: wo Hausübungen an ihre Grenzen stoßen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then explain the problem in your own words with one example.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann das Problem mit eigenen Worten und einem Beispiel erklären.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then explain the problem in your own words with one example and say what it leads to.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann das Problem mit eigenen Worten und einem Beispiel erklären und sagen, wozu es führt.

options.label: Time and pressure
options.text: Homework also has its limits. When teachers give too much, the most students work on their homework until late in the evening and have no time more for sport, music or friends. Many of them complain over stress, and tired students do not learn better.
options.textLong: Homework also has its limits. When teachers give too much, the most students work on their homework until late in the evening and have no time more for sport, music or friends. Many of them complain over stress, and tired students do not learn better. The next morning, some of them are almost asleep in the first lesson.
options.reject: Three typical mistakes: ‘the most students’ (→ most students), ‘no time more’ (→ no time left) and ‘complain over’ (→ complain about).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: the most students → most students, no time more (wörtlich „keine Zeit mehr“) → no time left, complain over → complain about.

options.label: Too much at once
options.text: {{[[However,]] homework also has clear limits.}} {{When several teachers}} give a lot on the same day, students may spend hours at their desks with no time for sport or friends. {{Tired students}} rarely learn anything new at eleven at night.
options.textLong: {{[[However,]] homework also has clear limits.}} {{When several teachers}} give a lot on the same day, students may spend hours at their desks with no time for sport or friends. {{Tired students}} rarely learn anything new at eleven at night, and the next morning they sit in class half asleep.
options.why: ‘However’ turns from the benefits to the problems. The example makes the problem easy to imagine.

options.label: Not fair for everyone
options.text: {{[[On the other hand,]] homework is not fair for everyone.}} Some students have parents who can explain fractions or check an English essay. Others have nobody to ask at home. {{In that case,}} homework tests the family, not the student.
options.textLong: {{[[On the other hand,]] homework is not fair for everyone.}} Some students have parents who can explain fractions or check an English essay. Others have nobody to ask at home, or they share a small room with younger brothers and sisters. {{In that case,}} homework tests the family, not the student.
options.why: A less obvious limit with a clear contrast between two groups and a short, strong last sentence.

steps.q: Body paragraph 3: how could homework work better?
steps.de: Dritter Inhaltspunkt: Vorschläge, wie Hausübungen besser funktionieren könnten. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add your own suggestion and say why it would help.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann einen eigenen Vorschlag ergänzen und begründen.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add two suggestions of your own and say why they would help.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann zwei eigene Vorschläge ergänzen und begründen.

options.label: Ask the teachers directly
options.text: Dear teachers, we would like to ask you for a few changes. Please give us shorter tasks with a clear aim, and plan the week together so that big projects do not all come at once. Thank you for reading this letter.
options.textLong: Dear teachers, we would like to ask you for a few changes. Please give us shorter tasks with a clear aim, and plan the week together so that big projects do not all come at once. Three good exercises are often enough, and sometimes we would like to choose between a text and a short video. Thank you for reading this letter.
options.reject: This is written like a letter to the teachers (‘Dear teachers’, ‘Thank you for reading this letter’), not a paragraph of a magazine article for teenage readers. An article explains the suggestions to its readers.
options.rejectDe: Das ist ein Brief an die Lehrer:innen, kein Absatz eines Artikels für Jugendliche.

options.label: Quality, not quantity
options.text: {{Homework would work much better if it were}} short and had a clear aim. Teachers could plan the week together so that big tasks do not all come at once. {{[[Instead of]] ten similar exercises,}} three good ones are often enough.
options.textLong: {{Homework would work much better if it were}} short and had a clear aim. Teachers could plan the week together so that big tasks do not all come at once. Now and then, students could choose between a written text and a short video. {{[[Instead of]] ten similar exercises,}} three good ones are often enough.
options.why: The topic sentence turns from the problems to the solutions. ‘Instead of’ compares the old way with a better one.

options.label: What students can do
options.text: {{Luckily, students themselves can make homework work better.}} {{[[While]] it is tempting to}} leave everything until Sunday evening, a fixed time each afternoon makes the work feel smaller. {{Another good habit is to ask}} the teacher early when something is unclear.
options.textLong: {{Luckily, students themselves can make homework work better.}} {{[[While]] it is tempting to}} leave everything until Sunday evening, a fixed time each afternoon makes the work feel smaller. {{Another good habit is to ask}} the teacher early when something is unclear. A quick question on Monday can save hours on Thursday.
options.why: ‘Luckily’ turns from the problems to the solutions. ‘While’ admits a temptation that every reader knows.

steps.q: How do we end the article?
steps.de: Der Schluss beantwortet die Frage des Artikels und rundet ihn ab. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then complete the ending in your own words with a clear message.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Schluss mit eigenen Worten und einer klaren Botschaft fertigschreiben.
steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then complete the ending in your own words: sum up both sides and end with a clear message.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann den Schluss mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben: beide Seiten zusammenfassen und mit einer klaren Botschaft enden.

options.label: A balanced answer
options.text: {{So, is homework a help or a headache?}} The honest answer is: it can be both. {{[[Despite]] its limits,}} it is worth doing if it is well planned.
options.textLong: {{So, is homework a help or a headache?}} The honest answer is: it can be both. {{[[Despite]] its limits,}} it is worth doing when tasks are short and well planned. That way, it helps us far more than it hurts.
options.why: Asks the main question once more and gives a balanced answer that sums up benefits, limits and suggestions.

options.label: An honest ending
options.text: Let’s be honest: homework will never be anyone’s favourite hobby. {{[[Yet]] if teachers and students plan it together,}} it can turn from a late-night headache into a real help.
options.textLong: Let’s be honest: homework will never be anyone’s favourite hobby. It takes time, and sometimes far too much of it. {{[[Yet]] if teachers and students plan it together,}} it can turn from a late-night headache into a real help.
options.why: A friendly, honest tone. The last sentence brings together the problems, the benefits and the suggestions.

steps.q: Now that the article is finished, which title do we choose?
steps.de: Der Titel kommt zuletzt und soll neugierig machen und zum Inhalt passen.
steps.own: Short and catchy: make teenagers want to read the article.
steps.ownDe: Kurz und treffend: Der Titel soll Jugendliche neugierig auf den Artikel machen.

options.label: A question with two sides
options.why: Short, catchy and it shows both sides of the topic.

options.label: A short slogan
options.text: Less is more: the homework question
options.why: A well-known phrase that makes readers curious about our answer.

options.label: A direct question
options.why: A direct question that every student wants to see answered.

checks.en: A title that makes readers curious
Each content point has its own body paragraph, in the order of the task
An introduction with a hook, not words copied from the task
All three content points: benefits, limits, suggestions
Each body paragraph opens with a topic sentence linked to the paragraph before
Contrast linkers really show a contrast (however, although, while …)
Neutral, friendly register for teenage readers

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam einen Artikel (A2+/B1) über Nutzen und Grenzen von Hausübungen mit drei Inhaltspunkten und übt dabei Linking words, die einen Gegensatz oder eine Einschränkung ausdrücken (although, however, on the other hand, while …).
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen (eine Garnitur pro Person), Hefte bereitlegen. Beamer im Vollbild. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5 min pro Absatz, bei Bedarf +1. Die Aufgabe am Beamer enthält alles Nötige.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum rechts oben, darunter „Article“ als Überschrift (wie am Beamer). Dann 2 Zeilen für den Titel frei lassen, der Titel kommt zuletzt. Fünf Absätze, jeder beginnt nach einer Leerzeile; am Rand stehen die Randwörter Intro, Body 1, Body 2, Body 3, Conclusion. Linking words für Gegensätze grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: Volltext kurz (50 min): 5 min Aufgabe lesen, 6 Entscheidungen (fünf Absätze, zum Schluss der Titel) à ca. 2 min, Abschreiben ca. 20 min, 5 min Checkliste. Volltext lang (ca. 60 min): dieselben 6 Entscheidungen, jeder Absatz ist etwas länger, Abschreiben ca. 25–30 min. In einer Doppelstunde die restliche Zeit für die Besprechung der Fallen nutzen und die Hausübung zu zweit beginnen. Gerüst kurz (realistisch ca. 60 min): 5 min Aufgabe; pro Absatz 1 min Entscheidung, 5–6 min eigenes Schreiben, 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell; Titel 2 min, am Ende 5 min Checkliste. In einer 50-Minuten-Stunde den Schluss noch abstimmen und das Gerüst abschreiben lassen; Schluss fertigschreiben und eigenen Titel finden als Hausübung. Gerüst lang (ca. 70 min): gleicher Ablauf, pro Absatz 1–2 min mehr für das längere eigene Schreiben. In einer Doppelstunde danach eine Vergleichsrunde zu zweit.
teacher.traps: Introduction B (LSR): Aufgabenstellung fast wörtlich übernommen, kein Einstieg. Body 1 C (CC): However leitet einen zweiten Vorteil ein, On the other hand eine Zustimmung, beide ohne echten Gegensatz. Body 2 A (LSA): the most students, no time more, complain over. Body 3 A (TA): als Brief an die Lehrer:innen geschrieben („Dear teachers“, „Thank you for reading this letter“) statt als Absatz eines Artikels für Jugendliche, falsche Textsorte. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Aufbau: Jeder Text hat genau fünf Absätze (Einleitung, drei Hauptteil-Absätze, Schluss), und jede Entscheidung ist ein ganzer Absatz. Die lange Fassung hat dieselben Entscheidungen, nur sind die Absätze länger. Fokus: markiert sind Linking words für Gegensatz und Einschränkung; das einfache „but“ wird nicht markiert. Nach der CC-Falle in Body 1 lohnt eine Minute an der Tafel: Welche Linking words hätten gepasst (In addition, In fact)? Body 2 zeigt gleich danach, wie However und On the other hand richtig einen Gegensatz einleiten. Für die Namenslücke nur erfundene Vornamen verwenden, keine Namen von Mitschüler:innen oder Lehrer:innen. Differenzierung: Schnelle schreiben im Gerüst-Modus einen zusätzlichen Satz mit einem anderen Gegensatz-Linker (whereas, nevertheless). Hausübung: zweite Fassung mit zwei anderen Entscheidungen oder ein Brief an die Redaktion der Schulzeitung mit der eigenen Meinung.
